learning_outcomes.text: Gaining the ability to determine the stress-strain, strain relations, and to apply the Generalized Hook's law

Gaining the ability to evaluate the Euler bending theory and to determine stress and strain relations for bending, to construct Mohr's Circles and to determine the stresses for different axes and principal axes

To gain the ability to determine the stability of structures for beams in case of buckling, to analyze critical stresses under different boundary conditions, to determine the maximum external loads that can be applied, to dimension and to select materials

Gaining the ability to learn the failure theories for brittle and ductile materials, to determine the safety coefficients of the designs according to the failure theories, whether they are safe in strength or not.
Gaining the ability to write project, designing and analyzing the mechanical systems

syllabus_topics: Introduction, General Principles of Mechanical System Design
Creating student groups, determination of the project topics
Axial/Shear Stress, stages in design, uncertainty, factor of safety
Three-dimensional stress analysis, generalized Hook's law, Anisotropy
Bending in Beams, Bending theory, deflection of beams
Stress at different axes and principal axes
Stress at different axes and principal axes
Buckling analysis in columns, Euler Theory, Evaluation and presentation of selected group projects
Static design criteria, damage theory for ductile materials, applications, Evaluation and presentation of selected group projects
Static design criteria, damage theories for brittle materials, applications, Evaluation and presentation of selected group projects, Fatigue, In-Class Project Evaluation
